Where it began

Suryakumar Yadav was born in Bombay on 14 September 1990. At ten he joined a cricket camp in the BARC colony in Mumbai, and from there he moved to the academy run by Dilip Vengsarkar, the former India batter, and on through the city's age-group sides. After school at Atomic Energy Central School he took a commerce degree at Pillai College and played his club cricket mostly for Parsi Gymkhana.

He first played for Mumbai in February 2010 and made his first-class debut against Delhi that December. In the 2011–12 Ranji Trophy he was Mumbai's leading scorer with 754 runs, and that year the BCCI named him its best Under-22 cricketer. He later played his part in the Mumbai side that won the 2015–16 Ranji Trophy, with 788 runs.

The player

His Test career was a single match, against Australia at Nagpur in February 2023, in which he made 8. The shorter game was where he made his name. In his first innings for India, in March 2021, he hit the very first ball he faced for six, the first Indian to do that in T20 internationals. He made four T20I hundreds, held the top place in the world T20I batting rankings from October 2022 to June 2024, and was the ICC's T20I Cricketer of the Year in 2022 and 2023.

He was part of the side that won the 2024 T20 World Cup, and in the final his catch near the boundary in the last over removed David Miller as India won by seven runs. Then as captain he led India to the 2025 Asia Cup and the 2026 T20 World Cup, the third Indian captain to lift that trophy.

What made him special

He seemed to have every shot there is, using his wrists to send the ball to all parts of the ground, scoops over fine leg included. That range earned him the name Mr. 360. He liked to attack from the very first ball instead of taking time to settle in.

The five-day game saw only a glimpse of him. One Test and one innings make a short story, but it means he can always say he wore the whites for India.

Away from the middle

He was known everywhere by his initials, SKY. In the Indian Premier League he won the title with Kolkata Knight Riders in 2014 and with Mumbai Indians in 2019 and 2020, and in 2023 he had his best season, with 605 runs and his first IPL hundred. He never lost his love of club cricket either, turning out for Parsi Gymkhana between bigger matches.

And finally

For a man who began his international career by hitting his first ball for six, his eight Test runs may be the most patient figure he ever put together.
